title: ASTU 2nd Round Model Exit Exam
source: ASTU Software Engineering — 2nd Round Model Exit Examination (2hr, 100 MCQs)

focusGuide.C++: Syntax, pointers, references, memory, file I/O, operators, control flow.
focusGuide.Data Structures: Stacks, queues, trees, arrays, graphs, recursion, complexity.
focusGuide.Java / OOP: Encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance, polymorphism, IDE tools.
focusGuide.Web Development: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, PWA, MVC, web servers, dynamic sites.
focusGuide.Android: Manifest, components, fragments, threading, resources, broadcast receivers.
focusGuide.Database: SQL DML, normalization, keys, cardinality, referential integrity.
focusGuide.Operating Systems: Scheduling, paging, threads, processes, security, deadlock.
focusGuide.Software Engineering: SDLC models, CASE tools, incremental development, RAD.
focusGuide.Requirements Engineering: Elicitation, SRS, scope, stakeholder bridge, analysis phase.
focusGuide.Software Architecture: Architecture docs, quality attributes, abstraction levels, scalability.
focusGuide.Project Management: PERT, Scrum, CMMI, maintenance types, risk mitigation.
focusGuide.Software Testing: Unit testing, coverage, early testing, data-driven testing.
focusGuide.Software Maintenance: Code smells, technical debt, ripple effect, data clumps.
focusGuide.Networking: TCP/IP, subnetting, routing protocols, OSI layers, firewalls.
focusGuide.AI / ML: Deep learning, gradient descent, supervised/unsupervised, overfitting, metrics.

questions.text: Which one of the following is a valid identifier name in C++?
questions.concept: Key idea (C++): __account

questions.text: Identify the correct C++ control statement used to test more than one condition from the given alternatives.
questions.concept: Key idea (C++): switch

questions.text: Which one of the following is the correct syntax for defining a reference variable y to a variable x assuming that x is declared as int (that is, int x;)?
questions.concept: Key idea (C++): int &y=x;

questions.text: One of the following operators is used to dynamically allocate memory in C++.
questions.concept: Key idea (C++): new

questions.text: One of the following is a scope resolution operator in C++>
questions.concept: Key idea (C++): ::
Key idea (C++): Welcome
Key idea (C++): 10 21 21
Key idea (C++): 30 40

questions.text: Which of the following correctly dynamically allocates memory for an array of 10 integers in C++?
questions.concept: Key idea (C++): int *arr = new int[10];

questions.text: Which mode should be used to open a file for both reading and writing in C++?
questions.concept: Key idea (C++): ios::in | ios::out

questions.text: Which of the following is used to implement recursion?
questions.concept: Key idea (Data Structures): Stack

questions.text: Which of the following data structures allows deletion at both ends but insertion at only one end?
questions.concept: Key idea (Data Structures): Dequeue

questions.text: Which of the following is not a characteristic of arrays?
questions.concept: Key idea (Data Structures): Dynamic resizing

questions.text: Which of the following is true about a circular queue?

options.text: It is a linear data structure
It overcomes the limitation of linear queue
It allows insertion at both ends

questions.concept: Key idea (Data Structures): It overcomes the limitation of linear queue

questions.text: Which of the following is not a type of tree traversal?
questions.concept: Key idea (Data Structures): Reverseorder

questions.text: Which of the following is not a linear data structure?
questions.concept: Key idea (Data Structures): Graph

questions.text: A developer argues for using Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) over procedural programming for a national health system that will grow, integrate with other systems, and require frequent updates. Which key advantage of OOP best supports this argument?
questions.concept: Key idea (Java / OOP): Better modularity and maintainability

questions.text: In an integrated development environment (IDE), a programmer steps through the execution of a program line by line while inspecting variable values to understand why a logical error occurs during runtime. Which IDE feature is the programmer primarily using?
questions.concept: Key idea (Java / OOP): Debugger

questions.text: A software architect emphasizes designing classes that represent concepts in the problem domain rather than focusing on implementation details. This allows developers to reason about the system at a higher level of understanding. Which object-oriented concept is being emphasized?
questions.concept: Key idea (Java / OOP): Abstraction

questions.text: Consider a banking application where the account balance must not be modified directly by external classes to prevent unauthorized transactions. The developer hides the balance variable and allows access only through controlled methods. Which object-oriented concept is primarily used to achieve this protection?
questions.concept: Key idea (Java / OOP): Encapsulation

options.text: It prevents unauthorized direct access to sensitive data

questions.concept: Key idea (Java / OOP): It prevents unauthorized direct access to sensitive data

questions.text: Which programming language is mainly used for client-side scripting to add interactivity to web pages?
questions.concept: Key idea (Web Development): JavaScript

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the role of a web server?

options.text: Stores and processes client requests and delivers web resources

questions.concept: Key idea (Web Development): Stores and processes client requests and delivers web resources

questions.text: Which combination correctly represents a typical web technology stack?
questions.concept: Key idea (Web Development): HTML, CSS, JavaScript

questions.text: Which shorthand property correctly sets margin-top and margin-bottom to 20px and margin-left and margin-right to 10px?
questions.concept: Key idea (Web Development): margin: 20px 10px;

questions.text: Which CSS rule ensures that padding and border are included in an element's total width and height?
questions.concept: Key idea (Web Development): box-sizing: border-box;
Key idea (Web Development): The nearest positioned ancestor

questions.text: When implementing Progressive Web App (PWA) features, which combination provides the BEST offline experience?
questions.concept: Key idea (Web Development): Service Worker + Cache API
Key idea (Web Development): 300px

questions.text: What happens when a user requests a page on a dynamic website?

options.text: The server sends a pre-built HTML file
The server generates the HTML on the fly using server-side scripts
The browser automatically creates the HTML

questions.concept: Key idea (Web Development): The server generates the HTML on the fly using server-side scripts

questions.text: What is the primary purpose of the AndroidManifest.xml file?

options.text: To store the visual layout of the application screens
To contain the Java/Kotlin source code for business logic
To manage the local SQLite database versioning
To define the essential information about the app for the Android system

questions.concept: Key idea (Android): To define the essential information about the app for the Android system

questions.text: What does the "R" file in Android development represent?

options.text: A file containing the Raw assets like MP3s
A dynamically generated class containing resource IDs
The Runtime configuration for the Dalvik Virtual Machine
The Repository link for Gradle dependencies

questions.concept: Key idea (Android): A dynamically generated class containing resource IDs

questions.text: In mobile computing, what is the role of a "Broadcast Receiver"?

options.text: To respond to system-wide announcement notifications
To navigate between different app screens
To play audio and video streams from a URL
To manage the synchronization of data with a remote server

questions.concept: Key idea (Android): To respond to system-wide announcement notifications

questions.text: Which of the following best describes "Fragments" in Android?

options.text: They are small portions of the SQLite database
They are modular sections of an activity with their own lifecycle
They are external libraries used for network requests
They are error messages shown when an app crashes

questions.concept: Key idea (Android): They are modular sections of an activity with their own lifecycle

questions.text: A developer wants to ensure that a long-running network task does not block the UI thread. What is the correct implementation strategy?

options.text: Run the task inside the onCreate() method directly
Increase the CPU priority of the main thread
Use a background thread or Coroutines/AsyncTask
Call Thread.sleep() before the network request

questions.concept: Key idea (Android): Use a background thread or Coroutines/AsyncTask

questions.text: Which of the following SQL command is used to add new records in database?
questions.concept: Key idea (Database): Insert

questions.text: What is composite attribute?

options.text: An attribute that can take more than one value for each entity instance
An attribute that can be split into components
An attribute that can be derived based on other attributes
An attribute that takes values from same domain

questions.concept: Key idea (Database): An attribute that can be split into components

questions.text: The cardinality of a relation in relational database refers to
questions.concept: Key idea (Database): The number of instances

questions.text: In relational data model, a relation schema is made of

options.text: Relation name and list of attributes
List of attributes and domain values
Entity set and list of attributes

questions.concept: Key idea (Database): Relation name and list of attributes

questions.text: Which of the following is SQL Data Manipulation (DML) command?
questions.concept: Key idea (Database): Update

questions.text: The primary purpose of referential integrity constraint is -------------------

options.text: To uniquely identify individual record from the two relations
To maintain the consistency among tuples in the two relations
Ensuring within each tuple, the value of each attribute is from same domain
To prevent data redundancy and avoid insertion anomalies in a database

questions.concept: Key idea (Database): To maintain the consistency among tuples in the two relations

questions.text: In which one of the following page replacement algorithms it is possible for the page fault rate to increase even when the number of allocated frames increases?
questions.concept: Key idea (Operating Systems): FIFO (First In First Out)

questions.text: A thread differs from a process because a thread:

options.text: Shares address space with other threads

questions.concept: Key idea (Operating Systems): Shares address space with other threads

questions.text: Which of the following increases overhead in an OS?
questions.concept: Key idea (Operating Systems): Context switching

questions.text: A process moves from Running to Waiting state when:
questions.concept: Key idea (Operating Systems): I/O operation is requested

questions.text: Zombie process is a process that:
questions.concept: Key idea (Operating Systems): Has terminated but PCB exists

questions.text: The primary goal of operating system security is to ensure:
questions.concept: Key idea (Operating Systems): Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability

questions.text: What is the primary emphasis of the spiral model?
questions.concept: Key idea (Software Engineering): Risk-driven development

questions.text: What best describes evolutionary prototyping?
questions.concept: Key idea (Software Engineering): Incremental development

questions.text: What is a software life-cycle?

options.text: A cyclic approach to software development
A phased approach to software development
The lifespan of cyclically developed software

questions.concept: Key idea (Software Engineering): A phased approach to software development

questions.text: What activities are performed during incremental software construction?

options.text: Detailed design and coding of classes in a system subset
Detailed design, coding, and unit testing of classes in a system subset
Coding and unit testing of classes in a system subset
Unit and integration testing of classes in a system subset

questions.concept: Key idea (Software Engineering): Detailed design, coding, and unit testing of classes in a system subset

questions.text: If you need to develop software within a strict deadline with unlimited budget, which development model would you choose?
questions.concept: Key idea (Software Engineering): RAD (Rapid Application Development)

questions.text: Which type of CASE tools support early process activities like requirements and design?
questions.concept: Key idea (Software Engineering): Upper-CASE

questions.text: Requirements Engineering mainly acts as a bridge between_______.
questions.concept: Key idea (Requirements Engineering): Stakeholders and developers

questions.text: Which phase of SDLC is most directly supported by Requirements Engineering?
questions.concept: Key idea (Requirements Engineering): Analysis

questions.text: Poor requirements engineering most commonly leads to_______?
questions.concept: Key idea (Requirements Engineering): Cost overruns and project failure

questions.text: A large organization plans to implement a new enterprise resource planning system. The system definition document describes the overall system context, boundaries, and how it aligns with organizational goals. What is the primary purpose of preparing such a document before detailed design begins?

options.text: Define overall system scope and context

questions.concept: Key idea (Requirements Engineering): Define overall system scope and context

questions.text: Requirements Engineering contributes to project success mainly by:
questions.concept: Key idea (Requirements Engineering): Clarifying expectations early

questions.text: Which artifact best represents architectural decisions?
questions.concept: Key idea (Software Architecture): Architecture documentation

questions.text: Which factor has the greatest long-term impact on system evolution?
questions.concept: Key idea (Software Architecture): Architectural structure

questions.text: Architecture decisions are difficult to change because they:
questions.concept: Key idea (Software Architecture): Affect multiple quality attributes

questions.text: Which stakeholder is MOST concerned with scalability?
questions.concept: Key idea (Software Architecture): Architect

questions.text: Architecture differs from design mainly by its:
questions.concept: Key idea (Software Architecture): Level of abstraction

questions.text: The PM decides to use PERT for the new feature's estimation. If the Optimistic time is 4 days, Most likely is 7 days, and Pessimistic is 16 days, what is the expected duration?
questions.concept: Key idea (Project Management): 8 days

questions.text: Which management activity is most critical when the team lead suddenly resigns during the "Execution" phase?
questions.concept: Key idea (Project Management): Risk Mitigation

questions.text: The team is using a "Scrum" framework. During the Sprint Review, the customer realizes the UI is not intuitive. Which SPM document was likely poorly defined at the start?
questions.concept: Key idea (Project Management): Software Requirement Specification (SRS)

questions.text: Management wants to add a new "Real-time Analytics" dashboard to the existing system. This falls under:
questions.concept: Key idea (Project Management): Perfective Maintenance

questions.text: Which model provides a framework for "Continuous Process Improvement" in software organizations?
questions.concept: Key idea (Project Management): CMMI (Capability Maturity Model Integration)

questions.text: Why is software testing crucial in the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC)?

options.text: It ensures that the software functions correctly and meets user expectations
It eliminates all defects from the software
It speeds up the development process
It guarantees the software will never fail

questions.concept: Key idea (Software Testing): It ensures that the software functions correctly and meets user expectations

questions.text: A finance company needs to verify that its fraud detection algorithm correctly flags suspicious transactions. The system must detect fraudulent activity while avoiding false positives. What testing approach is most suitable?
questions.concept: Key idea (Software Testing): Data-Driven Testing

questions.text: In the context of test case design, what is a key measurement used to assess test coverage?

options.text: Amount of time taken for testing

questions.concept: Key idea (Software Testing): Percentage of requirements tested

questions.text: Which principle of software testing states that testing should start as early as possible in the SDLC?
questions.concept: Key idea (Software Testing): Early testing

questions.text: In which scenario would unit testing be most beneficial?

options.text: Testing a complex integration between multiple services
Ensuring that an individual function in a program behaves correctly
Validating security vulnerabilities in a web application
Measuring system performance under peak load

questions.concept: Key idea (Software Testing): Ensuring that an individual function in a program behaves correctly

questions.text: In a legacy system, you find that changing a single requirement requires modifying 15 different classes. How would you evaluate this architectural state?

options.text: The system is exhibiting "Shotgun Surgery," indicating poor encapsulation
The system is exhibiting "Divergent Change," indicating a lack of cohesion
The system is following the Open-Closed Principle correctly
The system is optimized for high-performance execution

questions.concept: Key idea (Software Maintenance): The system is exhibiting "Shotgun Surgery," indicating poor encapsulation

questions.text: When evaluating the impact of "Feature Envy," what is the primary structural concern?

options.text: The method is excessively long and difficult to unit test
The method is more interested in the data of a class other than the one it is in
The method uses too many local variables, increasing memory consumption
The method is duplicated across multiple subclasses in a hierarchy

questions.concept: Key idea (Software Maintenance): The method is more interested in the data of a class other than the one it is in

questions.text: You are evaluating a system where "Technical Debt" is high. Which metric would best serve as an indicator of structural decay over time?

options.text: The total number of lines of code in the master branch
The ratio of comment lines to executable code lines
The increase in Cyclomatic Complexity relative to the number of new features added
The number of developers assigned to the maintenance phase

questions.concept: Key idea (Software Maintenance): The increase in Cyclomatic Complexity relative to the number of new features added

questions.text: A system has a high frequency of "Ripple Effect" defects. What is the most likely evaluation of its design?

options.text: High module cohesion and low coupling
High degree of global variable usage and tight coupling
Use of strict interfaces and dependency injection
Excessive use of inheritance rather than composition

questions.concept: Key idea (Software Maintenance): High degree of global variable usage and tight coupling

questions.text: Evaluate the "Data Clump" smell. What is the most effective way to judge if a group of variables constitutes a clump?

options.text: They are always passed together as parameters across different methods
They are all defined as static constants in a configuration file
They are all of the same primitive data type
They are used only within a single private method

questions.concept: Key idea (Software Maintenance): They are always passed together as parameters across different methods

questions.text: In the TCP/IP model, which layer corresponds to the Network Layer in the OSI model?
questions.concept: Key idea (Networking): Internet Layer

questions.text: What is the default subnet mask for a Class B IP address?
questions.concept: Key idea (Networking): 255.255.0.0

questions.text: Which protocol is used for resolving IP addresses to MAC addresses?
questions.concept: Key idea (Networking): ARP

questions.text: What is the primary purpose of the DHCP protocol?

options.text: To resolve domain names to IP addresses
To detect errors in data transmission
To assign IP addresses dynamically to devices

questions.concept: Key idea (Networking): To assign IP addresses dynamically to devices

questions.text: Which protocol is used for sending email from a client to a server?
questions.concept: Key idea (Networking): SMTP

questions.text: Which routing protocol uses the Dijkstra algorithm to find the shortest path?
questions.concept: Key idea (Networking): OSPF

questions.text: What is the purpose of a default gateway in a network?

options.text: To connect devices within the same subnet
To route traffic to devices outside the local network
To assign IP addresses to devices
To filter incoming and outgoing traffic

questions.concept: Key idea (Networking): To route traffic to devices outside the local network

questions.text: What is the purpose of a firewall in a network?

options.text: To assign IP addresses to devices
To resolve domain names to IP addresses
To filter incoming and outgoing traffic based on security rules

questions.concept: Key idea (Networking): To filter incoming and outgoing traffic based on security rules

questions.text: Which device operates at the Data Link Layer of the OSI model?
questions.concept: Key idea (Networking): Switch

questions.text: What is the main disadvantage of a bus topology?
questions.concept: Key idea (Networking): Single point of failure

questions.text: What is the maximum speed of a standard Ethernet network?
questions.concept: Key idea (Networking): 10 Mbps

questions.text: What does the term "deep" specifically refer to in the context of deep learning?

options.text: The complexity of the mathematical functions used
The amount of training data required for accuracy
The number of functions or layers in the network
The width of the hidden layers

questions.concept: Key idea (AI / ML): The number of functions or layers in the network

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an application of AI?

options.text: Weather prediction using fixed formulas only

questions.concept: Key idea (AI / ML): Weather prediction using fixed formulas only

questions.text: In gradient descent, what is the role of the momentum parameter?

options.text: It acts as a static step size that never changes
It ensures the weights are always initialized to zero
It is used to randomly drop units during the training process
It acts like a velocity of the step size to increase or decrease speed based on direction

questions.concept: Key idea (AI / ML): It acts like a velocity of the step size to increase or decrease speed based on direction

questions.text: Machine learning mainly focuses on:
questions.concept: Key idea (AI / ML): Learning patterns from data

questions.text: What is the main purpose of using Dropout during the training of a neural network?

options.text: To increase the learning rate of the output layer
To scale the prediction during training
To replace missing data points in the training set
To prevent overfitting by randomly setting some unit outputs to zero

questions.concept: Key idea (AI / ML): To prevent overfitting by randomly setting some unit outputs to zero

questions.text: Which type of learning uses labeled data?
questions.concept: Key idea (AI / ML): Supervised learning

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of supervised learning?
questions.concept: Key idea (AI / ML): Spam email classification

questions.text: Unsupervised learning is mainly used for:
questions.concept: Key idea (AI / ML): Finding patterns in unlabeled data

questions.text: Overfitting occurs when a model:
questions.concept: Key idea (AI / ML): Learns noise instead of patterns

questions.text: Which metric is commonly used to evaluate classification models?
questions.concept: Key idea (AI / ML): Accuracy
